title: Tenant affinity policy reconciliation race causes cross-environment routing and isolation breaches
creator: Marcus Liang
description: Production customer escalations reported that requests from Hosted tenants were intermittently routed to Dedicated pools and, in one case, to Private deployments violating tenant isolation guarantees. Impact included request failures (model mismatch errors), increased latency, and a breach of expected isolation for two enterprise customers during a peak traffic window. Root cause preliminary analysis: a race condition in the policy reconciliation service where global tiering policies and tenant-scoped affinity overrides were merged into the in-memory route cache non-atomically. When background syncs applied an incremental policy update while a tenant override write was in flight, cache entries transiently contained mixed policy attributes (region from global policy + tier from tenant override) leading to mis-evaluated route decisions. The issue manifests under load and during churn (policy updates, canary rollouts, burst scaling).
updates: 2026-03-10 08:14 - Pager alert triggered by increased 5xx to two enterprise customers (HostA Corp, FinanceCo). On-call investigated and opened this ticket (ENG-35244).

2026-03-10 09:00 - Short-term mitigation: blocked policy-sync daemon on control plane for 12 minutes to stop churn and rolled forward a targeted routing override for HostA to restore expected Dedicated affinity. Customer notifications sent. Latency stabilized for HostA; FinanceCo still seeing occasional misroutes.

2026-03-10 11:35 - Engineering root cause triage identified non-atomic cache merges in policy-reconciler (file: policy_reconciler/cache.go). Hypothesis: interleaved updates create partially-applied route records. Replicated locally with synthetic churn and tenant override workload.

2026-03-11 14:20 - Hotfix PR created to make cache updates atomic via versioned policy blobs and compare-and-swap (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4876). Added unit tests simulating concurrent policy writes.
2026-03-12 02:05 - Deployed hotfix to staging and ran a 6-hour soak with churn; no misroutes observed. Deployed to US-hosted region with canary serving 5% of traffic; telemetry looks stable.
2026-03-13 09:40 - Full rollout scheduled for 2026-03-13 11:00 UTC pending final QA. Postmortem doc skeleton created; incident review requested from SRE and Product.
2026-03-13 12:15 - Rollout completed to all regions. Monitoring indicates misroute rate returned to normal baseline. Closing mitigation path, moving to remediation and durable tests.
mitigation: Immediate: suspended background policy-sync for affected control-plane shard to stop churn and avoid further inconsistent cache states.
Targeted override: applied tenant-scoped explicit routing override for HostA and FinanceCo until fix validated.
Rollback: temporarily disabled new canary features that increased policy update churn (feature flags).
qa_steps: 1) Run the policy-reconciler concurrency test harness (tools/policy_test_harness) with 100 tenants and 30% churn for 30 minutes; assert zero mixed-attribute cache entries.
2) End-to-end staging test: simulate tenant override writes while performing global policy rollouts; confirm routed endpoints never cross environment boundaries (Hosted->Dedicated/Private).
3) Chaos test: restart policy-sync daemon mid-update to ensure CAS logic preserves previous valid snapshot and recovers cleanly.
4) Customer regression: run replay of HostA production traffic against staging using copied policy state; validate 0 misroutes and latency within SLA.
next_steps: Merge and monitor: finalize additional telemetry to detect mixed-policy attributes at the time of routing decision, include alerting for >0.1% occurrence.
Hardening: add end-to-end integration tests in CI that assert isolation invariants across hosted/dedicated/private for policy changes.
Postmortem: complete postmortem with timeline, triggering conditions, and remediation plan; present to R&D leadership and SRE guild.
Backfill: review other caches that perform incremental merges (quota cache, region-mapping cache) for similar race patterns and apply the same versioned-blob pattern.
Customer follow-up: coordinate with CS to provide affected customers a technical summary and compensation review.
